chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning

A man dies and there are no ones with him except women. He said: his wife washes him, because she is still connected to him during the waiting period ('iddah). But when she dies, he does not wash her, because he is not from her in a waiting period.

Because the intended meaning of his statement عليه السلام, 'when she dies, he does not wash her,' is that he does not wash her while she is stripped of her clothes; for we only allow that he wash her from beneath the clothing, and most of the preceding narrations indicate this.

And the difference between the man and the woman in this matter is that the woman may wash the man unclothed, although what is more virtuous and preferable is that she cover him and then wash him. It is not the same for the man, because it is not permissible for him to wash her except from behind the clothing.

key_terms.الثِّيَابِ: the garments through or beneath which washing may be performed
key_terms.الْأَفْضَلُ: what is more virtuous or preferable
key_terms.تُغَسِّلُهُ: she performs the ritual washing of the deceased upon him
key_terms.عِدَّةٍ: the waiting period that has legal relevance after death

ai.seo_question: Can a husband or wife perform the ghusl of their deceased spouse in Shi'a fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling on a spouse washing the deceased spouse. It explains that a wife may wash her deceased husband, while the husband may only wash his deceased wife from beneath her clothes, and this distinction is supported by the transmitted narrations.
